# Known actor indicators

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-indicators.mjs from src/rules/indicators.json. Edit that file and run the script; do not edit this page. -->

Host indicators that vendors published for named macOS malware families, in the forms a process capture can show: code-signing team and signing IDs, file and plist paths, and strings in a command line. File hashes and network indicators beyond what appears in an argument are left out on purpose: a capture holds neither. Each entry names its source and how sure it is. high = read in the report's own page text, or quoted exactly in Objective-See's reproduction of it; medium = read only through a summarizing fetch, or from a single secondary page. Severity is high only for a high-confidence, distinctive indicator. An absence of matches proves nothing: indicators age, and a family changes its names between samples. Chollima names are CrowdStrike's: the cited reports say DPRK, Lazarus or BlueNoroff.

Last updated 2026-11-17. `~/` is any user's home folder; `*` is any characters inside one path segment; `**/` is any number of folders; a trailing `/` means the folder and everything in it. Paths compare case-insensitively after /private/tmp, /private/var and /private/etc are written as /tmp, /var and /etc. kind `plist` is a launch plist file name, matched in /Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons and ~/Library/LaunchAgents. kind `argv` is a whole word in a command line, never argv[0].

## How to use it

- `mac-triage.sh` (section 10) looks for the **paths, launch plists, signing teams and signing IDs** below on this Mac and prints each match with its family. It cannot read command lines (they are off limits), so the *command-line word* entries are for a Ficus capture.
- A match with a **high** entry is a finding at level 3 of *Choosing the verdict* (`reading-the-result.md`); a match with a **medium** entry is level 2. Say which family and which entry, and quote the source.
- **No match proves nothing.** A family renames its files between samples, a list ages, and a Mac can be compromised by a family that is not here. Never say a Mac is clean because this list found nothing.
- Never use an indicator from memory. If this page is not in front of you, say the check was not done.
- **Attribution is the vendor's, with its own confidence.** Where a family's actor is tentative or not named, the table says so; do not tell the person a state actor is behind it unless the row says so.

## ChillyHell

**Actor:** UNC4487 (Mandiant's report is not public; Jamf says a Team ID matches Mandiant's sample). **Attribution:** vendor-attributed, not independently confirmed.

Modular macOS backdoor, signed and notarized under developer certificates that Apple later revoked. Persists as an Apple-lookalike launch plist, or in a shell profile.

| Kind | Value | Severity | Confidence | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| signing team | `R868N47FV5` | high | high | Signed chrome_render and the newer applet sample; revoked. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/chillyhell-a-modular-macos-backdoor/ |
| signing team | `F645668Q3H` | high | high | Signed the notarized eDrawMaxBeta2023 sample; revoked. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/chillyhell-a-modular-macos-backdoor/ |
| launch plist | `com.apple.qtop.plist` | high | high | Apple does not ship a plist of this name in a user or /Library launch folder. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x84.html |
| path | `~/Library/com.apple.qtop/` | high | high | Install folder of the user-level backdoor (`qtop`). | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x84.html |
| path | `/usr/local/bin/qtop` | high | high | Backdoor binary of the root install. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x84.html |
| path | `/tmp/kworker` | med | medium | Downloaded module run from here and deleted about 5 seconds later. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/chillyhell-a-modular-macos-backdoor/ |

## FlexibleFerret

**Actor:** DPRK-aligned operators, the Contagious Interview operation (Jamf); CrowdStrike names this cluster Famous Chollima. **Attribution:** vendor-attributed.

A fake job interview tells the victim to paste a Terminal command that "fixes" the camera or microphone and stages a loader in /var/tmp.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| launch plist | `com.driver9990as7tpatch.plist` | high | high | LaunchAgent that runs the loader; Jamf also names it. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x84.html |
| path | `/var/tmp/macpatch.sh` | med | medium | Stage-2 script of the camera and microphone lure. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/flexibleferret-malware-continues-to-adapt/ |
| path | `/var/tmp/CDrivers.zip` | med | medium | Payload archive. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/flexibleferret-malware-continues-to-adapt/ |
| path | `/var/tmp/CDrivers/` | med | medium | Where the archive is extracted. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/flexibleferret-malware-continues-to-adapt/ |
| path | `**/MediaPatcher.app/` | med | medium | Ad-hoc signed decoy app. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/flexibleferret-malware-continues-to-adapt/ |
| path | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/us.zoom.ZoomDaemon.plist` | med | medium | Earlier variant, as SentinelOne described it (the plist's Label is com.zoom). Only in the user's folder: the real Zoom installer's system daemon has this name in /Library/LaunchDaemons. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x84.html |
| path | `/var/tmp/InstallerAlert.app/` | med | medium | Earlier variant: fake password-prompt app opened by the installer's postinstall script. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x84.html |

## Contagious Interview toolchain (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie)

**Actor:** DPRK (Jamf: a long-running campaign attributed to the DPRK; Unit 42: CL-STA-0240, moderate confidence); CrowdStrike names this cluster Famous Chollima. **Attribution:** vendor-attributed.

Trojanized meeting apps and installers, poisoned repositories (VS Code tasks, git hooks) and a Python backdoor kit staged in hidden folders.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| path | `~/.npl` | high | high | InvisibleFerret's first Python script, in the home folder. | https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/two-campaigns-by-north-korea-bad-actors-target-job-hunters/ |
| path | `/Volumes/MiroTalk/MiroTalk.app/Contents/MacOS/Jami` | high | high | Trojanized native BeaverTail meeting app run from its disk image. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x7D.html |
| path | `**/Contents/MacOS/.macos` | med | medium | A hidden Go program as an app's CFBundleExecutable: the trojanized installers' entry point. | https://www.jamf.com/blog/contagious-interview-trojanized-macos-installers/ |
| path | `~/.vscode/vscode-bootstrap.sh` | med | medium | Dropped by the VS Code tasks.json route. | https://opensourcemalware.com/blog/latest-contagious-interview-malware-campaign-abuses-microsoft-vscode-tasks |

| path | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.onedrive.launcher.plist` | med | medium | The Mach-O Man kit's LaunchAgent for a fake OneDrive binary (Bitso, which calls the actor Famous Chollima). | https://quetzal.bitso.com/p/north-koreas-safari-hunting-for-rats |

## KANDYKORN

**Actor:** DPRK, overlapping with the Lazarus Group; Elastic tracks the intrusion set as REF7001 (Lazarus corresponds to CrowdStrike's Labyrinth Chollima). **Attribution:** vendor-attributed.

Fake arbitrage-bot lure sent over Discord; a Python dropper stages SUGARLOADER, and persistence hijacks Discord.

| path | `/Users/Shared/FinderTools` | high | high | Python dropper saved in /Users/Shared. | https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-catches-dprk-passing-out-kandykorn |

| path | `/Applications/Discord.app/Contents/MacOS/.lock` | high | high | The genuine Discord binary, renamed when HLOADER takes its place. | https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-catches-dprk-passing-out-kandykorn |

## RustBucket

**Actor:** Lazarus Group, high confidence (Elastic); earlier attributed to BlueNoroff by Jamf (CrowdStrike: Stardust Chollima). **Attribution:** vendor-attributed.

An AppleScript stage-1 app fetches a Rust backdoor into /Users/Shared and persists as an Apple-lookalike LaunchAgent.

| Kind | Value | Severity | Confidence | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| path | `/Users/Shared/.pd` | high | high | Stage-2 binary saved by the stage-1 script. | https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/DPRK-strikes-using-a-new-variant-of-rustbucket |
| path | `~/Library/Metadata/System Update` | high | high | Persistent copy of the binary. | https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/DPRK-strikes-using-a-new-variant-of-rustbucket |
| launch plist | `com.apple.systemupdate.plist` | high | high | Apple-lookalike LaunchAgent. | https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/DPRK-strikes-using-a-new-variant-of-rustbucket |
| command-line word | `webhostwatto.work.gd` | high | high | C2 URL passed as the LaunchAgent's argument (network indicator). | https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/DPRK-strikes-using-a-new-variant-of-rustbucket |

**Actor:** DPRK, BlueNoroff (SentinelOne, as quoted by Objective-See); CrowdStrike names BlueNoroff Stardust Chollima. **Attribution:** vendor-attributed.

A lure app masquerading as a PDF persists through ~/.zshenv, guarded by a marker file.

| Kind | Value | Severity | Confidence | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| path | `/tmp/.zsh_init_success` | high | high | Marker file that stops the ~/.zshenv line from running twice. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x7D.html |
| path | `**/Hidden Risk Behind New Surge of Bitcoin Price.app/` | high | high | First-stage lure app. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x7D.html |
| path | `/tmp/growth` | med | high | Second-stage backdoor; the name is generic, so only this exact path counts. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x7D.html |

**Actor:** BlueNoroff (TA444), DPRK-linked (Huntress, as quoted by Objective-See); CrowdStrike names BlueNoroff Stardust Chollima. **Attribution:** vendor-attributed.

A fake Zoom update AppleScript fetches a stager with a spoofed curl user agent and installs a Nim loader as a root LaunchDaemon.

## Evasive Panda macOS downloader (Monlam watering hole, 2024)

**Actor:** Evasive Panda, also called BRONZE HIGHLAND and Daggerfly (ESET: high confidence). **Attribution:** vendor-attributed, high confidence.

A trojanized Tibetan-keyboard installer, signed with a development certificate that Apple revoked 18 days after signing, installs a downloader and a LaunchAgent.

| Kind | Value | Severity | Confidence | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| signing team | `2289F6V4BN` | high | high | Team ID of the Apple Development certificate that signed the Mach-O; revoked 2024-01-25. | https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/evasive-panda-leverages-monlam-festival-target-tibetans/ |
| path | `~/Library/Containers/CalendarFocusEXT/` | high | high | Install folder the postinstall script copies the Mach-O into. | https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/evasive-panda-leverages-monlam-festival-target-tibetans/ |
| launch plist | `com.Terminal.us.plist` | high | high | Persistence LaunchAgent. Its Label is empty in Objective-See's transcription, so only the file name is used. | https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/evasive-panda-leverages-monlam-festival-target-tibetans/ |
| path | `~/Library/SafariBrowser/Safari.app/Contents/MacOS/SafariBrower` | high | high | Where the downloaded next stage is run from; "SafariBrower" is the report's spelling. | https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/evasive-panda-leverages-monlam-festival-target-tibetans/ |

## MACMA

**Actor:** Possibly Daggerfly / Evasive Panda (Symantec: evidence "to suggest" it is part of the toolkit); Volexity deploys it under StormBamboo; Google TAG named no actor. **Attribution:** tentative.

Backdoor first seen in a 2021 watering-hole campaign against Hong Kong; persists as a user LaunchAgent.

| Kind | Value | Severity | Confidence | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| launch plist | `com.UserAgent.va.plist` | med | medium | LaunchAgent of the analysed samples (Objective-See's reproduction). | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x69.html |
| path | `~/Library/Preferences/UserAgent/lib/UserAgent` | med | medium | Implant binary the plist runs. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x69.html |

## GIMMICK

**Actor:** Storm Cloud (Volexity, 2022), which Volexity later renamed StormBamboo, also called Evasive Panda; Volexity does not say how sure it is of the link. **Attribution:** tentative.

Spyware that names its plist, binary and agent per sample, so only the plist suffix is stable.

| Kind | Value | Severity | Confidence | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| launch plist | `com.*.va.plist` | med | high | Volexity: the name of the binary, plist and agent varies per sample; the .va.plist suffix is the constant. | https://www.volexity.com/blog/2022/03/22/storm-cloud-on-the-horizon-gimmick-malware-strikes-at-macos/ |
| path | `/var/root/Library/Preferences/CorelDRAW/CorelDRAW` | med | medium | One analysed sample's install path. | https://objective-see.org/blog/blog_0x71.html |
